declared.title: The consequences of effortful emotion regulation when processing distressing material: A comparison of suppression and acceptance
declared.foundIn: agent contre-preuve, recherche Crossref / Europe PMC du 2026-11-22 (reports/feeling-bad-about-feeling-bad/counter-evidence.md) ; titre relevé sur Crossref par l'agent : contrôle d'identité plus faible

population: 89 healthy adults, United Kingdom, a distressing video

findings.text: Suppressing the feeling lowered the fear felt during a distressing video

support.sentence: Suppression (relative to control) led to reduced subjective experience of fear when viewing the video, but did not alter electrodermal (EDA) or heart rate (HR) response.

findings.text: Accepting did not help during the video and went with more negative affect a week later

support.sentence: These findings suggest, contrary to the current clinical zeitgeist, that emotion suppression can successfully lead to an ongoing down-regulation of emotion and memory, whereas acceptance may elevate subsequent emotionality.

limits: one experiment, about 30 people per group
